motion: Does the evil-god challenge undermine belief in a wholly good God?

bridges.claim: Comparative symmetry undermines confidence in wholly good God; no burden to establish actual evil-god existence.
Natural theology must not favor loving creation over malicious creation without a defended asymmetry.
Proposed intrinsic asymmetries require defended comparative grounds, not merely possible theories.
Distinguish objective moral status from the later loving-versus-malicious reframing and state any concessions.
Reverse theodicies and challenge comparative mixed-world expectations.
Test whether moral greatness requires a wholly good disposition rather than overcoming contrary desires.
Reject ambitious equal plausibility while accepting the limited challenge and broad theodicy reversibility.
Show a comparative reason to expect conscious life more from good God than evil God, with tentative scope.
Defend conditional metaphysical constraints as an intrinsic asymmetry without implying personal endorsement of every theory.
Separate objective evil under moral accounts from malice under the revised character challenge.
Defend a comparative mixed-world expectation rather than the assertion that torture is worst possible.
Explain dispositions, possible worlds and power versus desire in relation to divine goodness.
